prompt: A Vulkan renderer intermittently returns VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST during one compute-to-graphics workload on an NVIDIA GPU after a driver update. Diagnose the GPU crash using the exact GPU model, PCIe topology, OS/kernel, driver, Vulkan loader/runtime, application build, workload seed, validation-layer version, and kernel Xid logs. Reproduce the same submission first without changing the driver; enable Khronos validation/synchronization or GPU-assisted diagnostics as appropriate, preserve any VUIDs and Xids, minimize the command sequence, and use a driver-version or second-GPU control only after the application-level evidence is captured. Determine the narrowest supported layer—invalid application usage, driver/runtime, transport/platform, or physical device—and verify the fix or mitigation against the original workload without claiming a hardware defect from Xid/device-loss alone.

requirements: recorded NVIDIA GPU and PCIe/topology identity
recorded OS/kernel, NVIDIA driver, Vulkan loader/API, validation-layer, and app-build versions
fixed workload seed and reproducible command/submission capture
kernel/event log containing any Xid messages and application device-loss result

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The reproduction records GPU, topology, kernel/OS, driver, Vulkan runtime/API, validation-layer, app build, and workload identity before changing any layer.

Application valid-usage evidence is collected with the appropriate Khronos validation features, preserving VUIDs/debug output while acknowledging that validation instrumentation can perturb timing/performance.
Any NVIDIA Xid and VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST evidence is treated as diagnostic evidence rather than automatic proof of defective hardware, and competing app/driver/platform hypotheses are tested.

A minimized failing submission or other layer-discriminating reproducer is preserved, and the proposed fix/mitigation is rerun against both that reproducer and the original workload on a stated real GPU/driver configuration.
